title: First-order Horn rules: grounding and least models

based_on.title: Artificial Intelligence: Foundations of Computational Agents

summary: Ground first-order definite rules, construct their least term model, and distinguish infinite closure from finite rule evaluation.
abstract: If a road leads from one town to another, and an onward road reaches a third, a rule can infer that the third town is reachable from the first. First-order Horn rules express such inferences with variables, allowing one finite rule to describe many individual cases. After adjoining a fresh constant if necessary, replacing the variables by closed terms makes their consequences into a problem about sets of ground facts. Every definite rule theory has a least model on those terms, and its true ground facts are exactly the positive ground facts forced in every ordinary model. Repeatedly adding applicable conclusions constructs that least model, although functions can make the process continue through infinitely many stages. With finitely many constants and relations and no functions of positive arity, only finitely many ground facts are possible, yielding a terminating decision procedure for ground positive consequences.
